To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
foliar application of plant regulators and physical film-forming materials differentially alter growth and physiological responses to transient water deficit stress of pepper seedlings.

ABA and AVG treatments had differential effects on gas exchange, water status, and growth of pepper seedlings exposed to transient water deficit cycles, and that ABA was more effective than AVG and physical film-forming materials in improving water deficit tolerance.
foliar application of the plant hormone ABA, but not of the plant regulators AVG or the physical film-forming materials AS, TF, and VG, improved water deficit tolerance of young pepper seedlings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of chemical and physical plant regulators to reduce water loss of transplants during field establishment and the subsequent effects on growth, development, and water status of the plant.
the use of plant regulators and physical materials to improve the ability of vegetable transplants to survive transient water deficit stress.
improving plant survival after transplanting and is relevant to the vegetable transplant industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of ABA is the only treatment that improved the tolerance of pepper seedling to transient water deficit stress.
ABA and AVG are effective in reducing transpirational water losses, but the effect of ABA is more pronounced and long-term than the effect of AVG.
ABA, AVG, and AS are not suitable for field establishment of transplants, while TF and VG are not suitable to be used in field establishment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

foliar application of AVG or AS may be used for improving stand establishment of vegetable transplanted seedlings in the absence of water deficit, but ABA application should be considered when water deficit conditions are likely to prevail.
ABA, TF and VG were effective in reducing transpiration, but only ABA was able to improve the water status and growth of pepper seedlings exposed to transient water deficit stress.
ABA application to pepper transplants could improve plant establishment and survival in the field by increasing water use efficiency and delaying senescence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
foliar application of plant growth regulators or physical materials may be used to improve water use efficiency and plant survival during transient water deficits.
ABA is a promising chemical plant regulator for improving pepper seedling tolerance to water deficit stress.
ABA application is a promising tool for improving pepper transplant establishment in the field.
